output.brief: The fall in first-contact resolution is almost certainly due to the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25. Larger adjustments now go automatically to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% in the week of 14 April. Referred calls resolve at about 33%, against 82% for the rest. This closely matches the timing and size of the drop. New starters refer at the same rate as tenured agents (56% vs 53–54%). Tenured agents' FCR fell from about 75% to 67%, the same as the site, so the intake is not the cause. Tariff-enquiry call mix barely changed. Performance plans for the April intake would punish the wrong group, so don't do them. I'm less sure about the IVR and workload effects, because I did not examine them directly. Next step: agree a revised in-call credit limit with Finance, with post-call sampling of credits. Trial it on two teams for six weeks. Track FCR and the unsupported-credit rate. Finance has said it would accept this kind of trial. A rollout to everyone at once is premature. Rebuilding the dashboard is useful but not urgent.
